param: the lensfun/darktable ptlens RADIUS NORMALIZATION actually applied by the production warp, measured end-to-end on a real frame
hypothesis: PRE-REGISTERED. The optics ledger (optical_state_d2_granularity_matrix) recorded its px verdicts under a MIN-HALF-DIM normalization and explicitly flagged the convention as unpinned ('radius-normalization convention must be pinned from lensfun source before final px verdicts'); TOOLS.md asserts lensfun rescales hugin-convention coefficients internally, unverified by probe. Two mutually exclusive conventions: H-DIAG r=1 at the frame CORNER (half-diagonal, 3643 px here) -> every ptlens model has ZERO displacement at the corner by construction and all four fitted/pinned models AGREE exactly there; H-MINDIM r=1 at half the SHORT side (2020 px) -> the corner sits at r=1.80, far outside the CP support (r<=1.0) where the cubic EXTRAPOLATES, and the recorded model-pair divergence there is 3.7-16.5 px.
discriminator: the RADIUS at which the measured warp displacement crosses zero, on a real calibrated frame through the production path (darktable --style lensdist vs --style nodist, same frame). Only one of 2020 px / 3643 px can be it.
instrument: Siril (calibrate/debayer/savetif32/findstar open gate) + darktable-cli (the production warp, --style-overwrite --icc-type LIN_REC709 bpp=32) + install_lens_model.sh; cross-match of the tools' own star lists, displacement vs radius
why_it_decides_the_smear: the failed observable is CORNER-ONLY star smear created at the cross-set compose. Under H-MINDIM the corner is unconstrained extrapolation and different members carry different corner geometry; under H-DIAG the corner is the one radius where all models agree and the mechanism must be elsewhere.
verdict: H-MINDIM CONFIRMED, H-DIAG KILLED. MEASURED end-to-end through the production warp (seeded synthetic star-field fixture at sensor geometry 6064x4040, darktable --style lensdist vs --style nodist, Siril findstar, 150 dots at 400 px pitch so no match is ambiguous): fitting the measured radial displacement of all four models simultaneously gives RMS 4.47 px for Rn = half SHORT side (2020 px), 18.27 px for half long side, 22.22 px for half DIAGONAL; a FREE Rn lands at 2000 px (1% of 2020). The normalisation is HALF THE SHORT SIDE. CONSEQUENCE: the frame CORNER is at rho = 3643/2020 = 1.80 while hugin's control points constrain the fit only to rho <= 1.0 — the ptlens cubic EXTRAPOLATES 80% beyond its support exactly where the defect lives, so fits that are interchangeable inside the supported field are free to disagree at the corners. MODEL-PAIR DIVERGENCE, measured (px, radial, peak over field): s02-vs-s03 8.19, s01-vs-s03 6.24, s02-vs-pinned 6.27, s01-vs-pinned 4.91, s01-vs-s02 2.80, s03-vs-pinned 1.91 — peaking near rho ~ 1. The identity control (nodist) closes at median |tangential| 0.50 px, max |radial| 0.71 px. SUPERSEDES the caveat in optical_state_d2_granularity_matrix ('radius-normalization convention must be pinned from lensfun source'): it is pinned, by probe, and the min-half-dim convention that ledger's px numbers used is the correct one. Also corrects TOOLS.md's unprobed claim that lensfun 'rescales hugin-convention coefficients internally' — no rescaling is needed or observed; hugin's half-short-side convention IS lensfun's.

CORRECTS the compose-smear report's shorthand 'CP support only to rho <= 1.0': support is sparse but real out to ~1.5; it is the corner beyond 1.5 that is unconstrained.

hypothesis: PRE-STATED before opening the artifacts: if corner control points are simply never DETECTED, no refit strategy can constrain the corner and F2 needs a detection lever. If instead they are detected and then PRUNED, the fix is the prune ORDER and the existing frames already suffice.
instrument: scripts/darktable/cp_coverage.py over the three stages hugin already wrote for each fit (cps.pto raw -> clean.pto default cpclean -> strict2.pto strict cpclean x2), the SAME artifacts fit_lens_model.sh preserves; radius normalised by half the short side (the MEASURED lensfun convention)
verdict: PARTLY REFUTED BY A FOLLOW-UP TEST — corrected here rather than left standing. WHAT STANDS (measured): cpfind's raw control points DO reach the corner (rho_max 1.60-1.78 vs a corner at 1.80) and cpclean removes almost all of them (9.9%->0.0% beyond rho 1.50 on july31/set-01); and the destructive half is cpclean STEP 2 (whole-panorama), not step 1 — MEASURED by running each step alone on aug06/set-01's raw set: step 1 removes ONE point of 225 and keeps corner support (max 1.77, 5.6% beyond 1.5), step 2 alone reproduces the shipped result exactly (180, max 1.61, 1.9%). WHAT IS REFUTED: the MECHANISM I attributed it to — 'step 2 deletes corner points because a,b,c are not yet fitted'. Discriminating test: seed step 2 with a project that already carries a FITTED a,b,c (pto_template) and skip re-optimisation (cpclean -w -s). It removes the same population: 219 -> 183, rho_max 1.77 -> 1.65, 5.9% -> 2.7% beyond 1.5 — indistinguishable from the model-free prune. So the corner points have large residuals under ANY model: they are predominantly BAD MATCHES (cpfind SIFT on aberrated, low-SNR corner stars), not good constraints being wrongly discarded. The -n threshold is also exhausted: both-steps at n=3,4,5,6,8 all return the identical 178 points, so the removed population sits far beyond mean+8sigma. CONSEQUENCE: corner support cannot be won by reordering or relaxing the prune. It needs corner CORRESPONDENCES that are actually good — a detection/matching problem, not a pruning one.
verdict_superseded: DETECTION IS NOT THE PROBLEM — THE PRUNE IS. cpfind's raw control points DO reach the corner (rho_max 1.60-1.78 against a corner at 1.80; july31/set-01 puts 9.9% of its CPs beyond rho 1.5). The strict cpclean then removes essentially all of them: 9.9% -> 0.0% (july31), 4.5% -> 0.4% (set-02), 1.0% -> 0.0% (set-03), with rho_max falling 1.76->1.24, 1.78->1.50, 1.60->1.47. MECHANISM: cpclean prunes on residuals against the CURRENT model, and the staged optimise runs ROTATIONS ONLY before the prune — so the residual it judges comes from a model with NO distortion terms, and an unmodelled radial distortion's residual GROWS WITH RADIUS. The prune therefore deletes the largest-radius points systematically: the control points that would constrain the corner are removed BECAUSE the corner is not yet modelled. Self-defeating loop. COROLLARY, and it corrects a standing record: july31/set-01's refit was rejected as 'CP coverage radially BANDED, fit untrustworthy'. The banding was CREATED by this prune — its raw coverage was the BEST of any fit measured here. The rejection's conclusion (do not ship that fit) stands; its stated cause does not. CONSEQUENCE: the corner-true refit needs no new detection and no new frames — it needs the prune to run AFTER a,b,c are fitted, so corner points are judged against a model that can represent them.

param: the CP PRUNE ORDER in fit_lens_model.sh — one knob. Control arm = the shipped procedure (cpclean -> optimise ypr -> optimise abc, with the strict prune applied on the rotation-only model). Test arm = optimise ypr -> optimise abc -> strict prune ON THE abc MODEL -> re-optimise abc.
hypothesis: PRE-REGISTERED, with its numeric acceptance criterion FIXED BEFORE the run (scripts/darktable/cp_coverage.py CRITERION, committed): a fit is CORNER-TRUE iff rho_max >= 1.75 AND rho_p99 >= 1.60 AND at least 5% of control points lie beyond rho 1.50 AND n >= 100. Each threshold is placed against the measured census (every shipped fit: p99 1.43-1.48, max 1.47-1.51, 0.0-0.4% beyond 1.5) and the corner at rho 1.80. H: pruning after the abc fit retains the corner points that cp_prune_deletes_corner_support showed are detected and then discarded, and the resulting fit meets the criterion on the SAME frames.
control: the shipped fits and their preserved artifacts, untouched
acceptance: the criterion above on CP coverage, THEN the product-level measure: member separation (scripts/qa/member_separation.py) on a cross-set compose under the new model. A fit's own residual is NOT acceptance evidence — it is computed only where the control points are, and 0.02-0.10 px residuals accompanied 2.99 px of corner disagreement.
verdict:
FAILED its pre-registered criterion — reported, not worked around. Three prune variants on aug06/set-01, all measured against the criterion fixed before the run (rho_max>=1.75, rho_p99>=1.60, >=5% of CPs beyond rho 1.50, n>=100):
  shipped order (both cpclean steps first) . n=176 p99 1.56 max 1.65 2.8% -> PARTIAL
  model-first (pairwise, fit, whole-pano) .. n=183 p99 1.56 max 1.65 2.7% -> PARTIAL
  pairwise-only, no whole-pano prune ....... n=219 p99 1.62 max 1.77 5.9% -> TRUE, but the FIT on it is DEGENERATE (a=-1.02 b=3.03 c=-2.37 against shipped values ~0.001-0.02) — the outliers the whole-pano step removes are real, and the docstring's warning about the degenerate basin is confirmed.
So the corner-safe CP set and a physically sane fit are, on these data, mutually exclusive. No aug06 fit is corner-true, and the route to one is NOT in the prune (see cp_prune_deletes_corner_support's correction). The candidate records are kept as lens_fit_cand_f12/f16.json and lens_fit_candidate_cornertrue.json; the SHIPPED lens_fit.json was never touched. Sequence steps 3(july31 refit), 4(cross-night acceptance run) and 5(rebuild) are NOT started: they are all downstream of a corner-true fit that does not exist.
OBSERVED LIMIT, unchased: --frames=20 produced no cps.pto at all (cpfind wrote nothing on 190 full-scale pairs); 12 and 16 both completed.

hypothesis: PRE-STATED once two fits of the SAME set landed 3.26 px apart: if the fitting procedure's own run-to-run variance is comparable to the between-set differences, then the 0.47 px equivalence bound the per-set doctrine was adopted against cannot discriminate an optical state from a fit, and corner-true PER-STATE fitting (F2) is chasing a target the instrument cannot resolve.
instrument: the T1 arithmetic (ptlens displacement difference over the field, half-short-side normalisation), peak px over the CP-supported field rho<=1.55; four independent fits of aug06/set-01 (shipped mid-burst+strict-prune; as-written frames=12 default prune; as-written frames=12 corner-safe prune; as-written frames=16 default prune) against the three shipped per-set models

numbers.notable: aug06/set-01's as-written f12 refit sits 0.83 px from set-02's SHIPPED model and 3.26 px from set-01's own shipped model — a refit of a set agrees with ANOTHER set's model better than with its own

verdict: MEASURED: the per-set doctrine is NOT refuted — between-set differences are systematically larger (median 7.04 vs 3.22 px) — but the two distributions OVERLAP (same-set max 6.30 exceeds between-set min 4.01), and BOTH dwarf the 0.47 px equivalence bound by 7-23x. So 'all pairs exceed the 0.47 px bound' was never evidence of distinct optical states: ANY two fits exceed it, including two fits of one set. THE BINDING CONSEQUENCE: the fitted model's own reproducibility (+-3 px in the outer field, from frame-subset and prune choices alone) is AT THE SCALE OF THE DEFECT it must fix (2.99 px of corner member disagreement). Corner-true per-STATE fitting cannot be verified until the fit is reproducible to well inside that, so fit REPRODUCIBILITY is a prerequisite of F2, not a detail of it. SCOPE, stated: this measures the fit's coefficient reproducibility only. The product-level A/B that adopted per-set models for set-01 (off-axis 0.82 -> 0.48 px) is separate evidence measured on real stacks and is untouched by this.

param: ONE KNOB — the distortion source consumed at the COMPOSE. Control: the shipped route (members warped by darktable+lensfun under their own per-set model, then registered by homography alone) = the pair that BLOCKS at 2.99 px. Arm: the SAME two members, each plate-solved by Siril to SIP order 3 from the SKY, registered with `register -disto=` so each member's OWN astrometric distortion corrects its star positions and undistorts it on export.
hypothesis: PRE-REGISTERED. The industry-standard route for coadding heterogeneous exposures derives distortion PER IMAGE astrometrically (SWarp/TPV, PixInsight StarAlignment+ImageSolver, APP) rather than from a shared instrument model, and is therefore immune BY CONSTRUCTION to the failure measured here: there is no shared model for members to disagree about, because every member is mapped to the SKY by its own solution. H: applying each member's own SIP at registration collapses the member separation from 2.99 px toward the same-set floor (0.14-0.19 px). If it does, the per-set-model corner problem (F2) dissolves rather than needing a corner-true fit.
instrument: Siril seqplatesolve -order=3 (native, headless, MEASURED working on this class: 2/2 solved, 388/371 matched stars, residual sigx/sigy 0.96/0.85 and 0.99/0.93 px, positions agreeing with astrometry.net to 0.001 deg) + register -disto= + scripts/qa/member_separation.py
why_now: BACKLOG:`native-solve-and-sip` queued exactly this as the fitted-lens-model removal-condition test and it was never run; its stated acceptance measures were seqtilt off-axis + drift-axis stations, BOTH of which are now MEASURED BLIND to this defect class (docs/dead-ends.md). It is re-run here on the instrument that can see it.
verdict: REFUTED AS INVOKED — and the refutation is informative. Siril 1.4.4 CAN solve this class natively (MEASURED: seqplatesolve -order=3, 2/2 members solved, 388 and 371 matched stars, residual sigx/sigy 0.96/0.85 and 0.99/0.93 px, centres agreeing with astrometry.net to 0.001 deg, RA---TAN-SIP + A_ORDER 3 written into each member's own header). But `register -disto=` is a SHARED-SOLUTION facility, not per-image reprojection:   arm (each member undistorted by ITS OWN SIP, then composed) 3.99 / 6.42 / 6.19 px (centre/mid/outer) against the shipped lensfun control's 0.29 / 0.63 / 2.10 / 2.99 — WORSE, and worst at the CENTRE, which no distortion story explains. MECHANISM, isolated by a further one-knob probe: warping a SINGLE member by its OWN solution and composing it against its own unwarped self gives 8.50 / 9.45 / 6.76 px. The polynomial is not identity-preserving on its own — it only cancels when EVERY member shares the same solution, which is exactly Siril's documented use (`distortion terms from a previous platesolve solution`, applied to a sequence). Siril's own design therefore assumes ONE optical state per sequence — the same one-model-per-combine-family pattern, now confirmed as the tool's assumption rather than this repo's invention. SCOPE: this refutes the INVOCATION, not the architecture. The industry-standard operation is resampling each exposure onto a COMMON output WCS using its own full solution (CD matrix AND distortion), which is SWarp's model; Siril has no such command, and neither SWarp nor python `reproject` is installed here (SWarp is packaged for this distro at 2.41.5-3). ALSO RETIRED: the standing belief that Siril's internal solver cannot handle this class. It cannot handle single ULTRA-WIDE TRAILED frames — the measurement that established it — but STACKED members have round stars and solve fine. The belief had silently widened past its evidence.

question: Is Nikon's embedded per-shot distortion model the per-OPTICAL-STATE source that would replace the in-house hugin fit? TOOLS.md had recorded the coefficients as present-but-unpriced.
instrument: exiftool 13.55, headers only, one invocation over the whole archive: -r -ext NEF -csv -n over sessions/ (n=7702 frames; july14/july23/july31/aug06; 19 light sets + 4 dark sets), reading Nikon DistortionInfo (MakerNote tag 0x0005) RadialDistortionCoefficient1..3 plus PowerUpTime, LensPositionAbsolute, FocalLength, VignetteCoefficient1..3. Cross-checked against exiv2, LibRaw 0.22.1, dcraw; darktable 5.4.1 maker coverage read from src/common/image.h and confirmed against the installed binaries.
verdict: STATIC, NOT PER-STATE - the route does not replace the fit. MEASURED: exactly TWO distinct coefficient triples exist in 7702 frames. A=(0.01821231842,-0.01132106781,0.05938911438) covers 7355 frames including EVERY light set of all four nights; B=(0.01828289032,-0.01136207581,0.05913734436) appears in july31/darks only (347 frames). THE KILL: the july31 and aug06 members measured 4.07 px apart at the corner (cross_night_state_difference) carry BYTE-IDENTICAL coefficients, so adopting this model for both nights IS adopting a shared model and reproduces that failure by construction.
mechanism: The block latches per POWER-UP, not per optical state. Grouped by Nikon:PowerUpTime, 14 of 15 power-up cycles across four nights emit triple A; one emits B, and the VignetteInfo coefficients flip in that same power-up (VignetteCoefficient1 -4.667527199 -> -4.62051487), so the whole correction block is re-latched together. LensPositionAbsolute - the state field that DOES move - does not predict the coefficients: it spans -17..0, takes the value 0 in BOTH groups, and july31/set-01 holds 3 distinct lens positions under ONE triple. The corner difference between the two triples is order-independent (at rho=1 every term multiplies by 1) and equals the sum of the coefficient deltas: 2.222061e-04 * 3634.40 = 0.808 px, i.e. the model's ENTIRE range of motion over four nights is one fifth of the defect it would have to explain.
application_gap: MEASURED, and it is the harder blocker. DECODE: exiftool alone. exiv2 returns only Nikon3.VignetteControl, LibRaw 0.22.1 has zero 'distort' strings, dcraw reports nothing - and darktable/RawTherapee read maker notes THROUGH exiv2. APPLY: darktable's dt_image_correction_type_t enum is {NONE,SONY,FUJI,DNG,OLYMPUS,PANASONIC} with no NIKON, and RawTherapee PR#7100 (merged 5.11) implements the identical maker set - two independent projects at the same boundary. The installed darktable 5.4.1 carries DT_IOP_LENS_METHOD_EMBEDDED_METADATA and WarpRectilinear but cannot reach a Nikon NEF. Only live route is DNG opcodes, and the sole converter that writes them (Adobe DNG Converter) is proprietary and Windows/macOS-only (Wine-runnable); the free native one (dnglab) explicitly drops lens opcodes.
model_form: DOC (Adobe dng_sdk dng_lens_correction.h): WarpRectilinear radial w(r)=kr0*r+kr1*r^3+kr2*r^5+kr3*r^7, with r=1.0 anchored at the farthest corner of the active area and an invertibility constraint over that domain - so a manufacturer model is corner-defined BY CONSTRUCTION, which is exactly what the hugin fits cannot reach at rho=1.80. Nikon stores three rationals with denominator 2^20 at block offsets 0x14/0x1c/0x24; a FOURTH 2^20 rational at +0x40 that exiftool does not decode co-varies with them (74572/2^20=0.0711174 vs 74330/2^20=0.0708866) - plausibly the autoscale factor, unsettled. That Nikon's triple IS DNG's kr1..kr3 is UNVERIFIED COMMUNITY; the pixls.us reverse-engineering effort (t/36733) has derived no formula and no code, and names the exiv2 gap as its own blocker. NORMALISATION settled by arithmetic, not by document: under half-diagonal (rho=1 at corner) the model gives +6.6% corner stretch; under the repo's half-short-side convention the same coefficients give +197.8%, which is not a lens.
null_result: The on-rig attempt to MEASURE the model empirically is a CLEAN NULL. Design: every NEF embeds a full-size 6048x4032 in-camera JPEG with the correction applied, so its displacement field against a darktable 'nodist' render of the same NEF is the applied model. Executed with sep 1.4.1 and three matchers (polar-angle, centre-out bootstrap, patch phase-correlation). No correspondence exists to fit: the central translation vote, which must peak sharply since the warp is ~0 at the centre, gave 11 votes against a 99.9pct of 7 at every threshold from 4 to 50 sigma. MECHANISM, identified by direct inspection of matched 400x400 centre patches: the in-camera JPEG is dominated by 8x8 JPEG block artifacts, not stars - a 2.5 s ISO 1600 sub at 70 mm is sky-noise-dominated and the lossy 8-bit encode destroys the faint star field. This is a data limit, not a method limit, and it is the SAME limit that starved the hugin corner fit. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one frame from this body+lens at this focal length on a bright structured subject (daylight or moonlit landscape), where the in-camera JPEG carries real detail. Two minutes at the next acquisition; converts the model form from COMMUNITY to MEASURED.
scope: All 7702 frames are at 70 mm, so this measures 'static across nights, sets, focus positions and power-ups AT ONE FOCAL LENGTH'. A zoom-indexed table is untested here and near-certain to exist; a dataset at another zoom setting would get a different, equally static triple.
consequences: F2 is untouched - corner-support starvation and ~3 px fit reproducibility (75340bb) still gate multi-night combining, and the T-1 trade options (a)/(b)/(c) stand exactly as costed. What is bought: TOOLS.md's unpriced entry can be closed, and no future session need re-open it hoping the coefficients are per-shot. What survives: the embedded model as a candidate STATIC base model that reaches the corner - the one place the community lensfun profile measurably fails (paraxial centre band, july14 centre 5.30 vs perpendicular 3.60 px).
next_test_if_wanted: E0 GATE, cheap and decisive: convert ONE NEF with Adobe DNG Converter under Wine, read exiftool -v3 -OpcodeList3, compare WarpRectilinear kr0..kr3 against the MakerNote triple. PASS proves route (b) end-to-end AND hands route (c) the model form and normalisation that no public source has published. FAIL closes both routes for the cost of one file. Pre-registered: E0 PASS required before any pixel is warped by this model. E2 then has its answer pre-registered - both nights share coefficients, so a cross-night compose under this model should reproduce ~4.07 px, and landing at the 0.14-0.35 px floor instead would REFUTE the reading that 4.07 px is a physical state difference.

hypothesis: PRE-STATED after the owner's field correction that the generic (one-for-everything) model DID combine sets, cross-set and cross-night successfully: re-measure the load-bearing `cross_night_state_difference` cell independently, because it is the single number behind 'a shared model does not cross nights' and it was not measured by this session.
instrument: scripts/qa/member_separation.py (validated on six same-night cells against the owner's own eye verdicts), on freshly registered pairs; plus a bootstrap and a tail check on the raw per-star separations
verdict:
TWO findings, and the second limits the first.
1. THE ONE-KNOB COMPARISON IS ROBUST AND SUPPORTS THE OWNER. Same two nights, same member pair, only the model differing: ONE shared model beats TWO per-set models at EVERY zone — centre 0.41 vs 0.92, mid 1.09 vs 1.31, outer 2.07 vs 2.73, corner 3.38 vs 5.34 (rho>=0.70 binning). A single generic model is measurably the better cross-night configuration, which is what the owner's field experience says.
2. THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT VALIDATED FOR LARGE RE-AIM GEOMETRY, so no ABSOLUTE cross-night number from it should be trusted — including the 4.07 px that has been driving this arc. Its zones are CANVAS-radial, which equals FIELD-radial only when the members are near co-pointed (true for every cell it was validated on: 98-500 px offsets). Across a re-aim the canvas centre lies between two optical axes, so a canvas corner is at a different field radius in each member. Symptoms, measured: the profile goes NON-MONOTONIC (outer 2.07 worse than corner 0.71), the corner median swings 0.71 -> 3.38 on a 0.10 change of the zone bound, the distribution is heavy-tailed (median 0.71, p75 5.21, p90 5.92) and the bootstrap band is 0.55-3.89. My centre/mid/outer reproduce the prior session's X1 closely (0.41/1.09/2.07 vs 0.33/0.99/1.87); only the corner diverges, which is exactly the zone the geometry breaks.
CONSEQUENCE: `cross_night_state_difference`'s 4.07 px is DOWNGRADED from a measured fact to an instrument-limited estimate, and every conclusion resting on it — 'a shared family model does not cross nights', F1 demoted to same-night-only, F2 promoted as the multi-night requirement — loses its evidence. It is not refuted either; it is UNMEASURED. The fix is to bin by each member's OWN field radius via its own WCS rather than by canvas radius, and to re-run the cross-night cells on that.
